title: XDAT Holdings See Big Achievements
summary: Franklin Exponential Data ETF (XDAT) holdings Fortinet, Datadog Inc., and ZoomInfo have recently announced new achievements or offerings. Fortinet launched FortiNDR for enhanced cybersecurity, Datadog achieved AWS Education Competency, and ZoomInfo's data is now available in its Chorus platform. These developments are expected to impact the actively managed XDAT fund, which invests in companies benefiting from the growth and use of large datasets.

title: ADM’s flaxseed products ship globally
summary: The Archer-Daniels-Midland (ADM) plant in Red Wing, Minnesota, which began as Zumbro Linseed Company in 1902, continues to process flaxseed for global distribution. ADM, also founded in 1902, acquired the Red Wing facility in 1971, making it the company's last remaining flaxseed processing plant. The article details how flaxseed oil is used in industrial applications, supplements, and increasingly in human consumption, with the Red Wing team selling products like "Linsheen" and "Knwble Grwn" online.

title: Kroger to extend greater Columbus home delivery reach with Lockbourne facility
summary: Kroger has opened a new 61,000-square-foot delivery hub in Lockbourne, near Rickenbacker International Airport, to expand its home delivery services in greater Columbus and surrounding areas. This facility will serve customers up to 200 miles away in over 250 ZIP codes and expects to employ up to 200 workers. The move enhances Kroger's delivery capabilities, with its own associates handling deliveries, and represents an extension of its partnership with U.K.-based e-commerce company Ocado.

title: Quantrepreneurs: Wall Street Quants Who Left Trading to Build Startups
summary: This article profiles eight "quantrepreneurs"—quantitative finance professionals who transitioned from lucrative Wall Street trading careers at firms like Citadel and Renaissance Technologies to found or join tech startups. Inspired by Jeff Bezos, these individuals sought more impactful work, moving into diverse fields such as AI in insurance, medical technology, sustainable energy, decentralized finance, and real estate tech. Their stories highlight a growing trend of quants applying their analytical skills to real-world problems, often leveraging non-compete periods to explore entrepreneurial ventures.

title: To Promote 'Stranger Things,' These Businesses Developed an App That Lets You Order a Pizza With Your Mind
summary: To promote the fourth season of Netflix's "Stranger Things," Domino's partnered with WorkInProgress and Unit9 to launch a new "mind-ordering" app. This app allows users to order pizza using head movements, mimicking the telekinetic powers of the character Eleven. It also features a "Just for Fun" mode to explore the show's world and discover Easter eggs, building on Domino's history of innovative ordering methods.

title: Walmart is using its thousands of stores to battle Amazon for e-commerce market share
summary: Walmart is leveraging its extensive network of nearly 4,700 stores across the U.S. as "shoppable fulfillment centers" to boost its e-commerce market share and compete with Amazon. The retailer is transforming its physical locations into hubs for drone deliveries, automated online grocery order fulfillment, and direct-to-fridge drop-offs, aiming to provide faster and more efficient service. This strategy also involves wooing third-party sellers by offering fulfillment services from its stores and expanding its delivery and membership programs like GoLocal and Walmart+.

title: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy earned 6,474 times the median Amazon employee’s salary
summary: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy received a compensation package of nearly $213 million in 2021, which was 6,474 times the median Amazon employee's salary of $32,855. This high compensation was primarily due to a special restricted stock award tied to his promotion to CEO. While several other Fortune 500 CEOs also earned significantly more than their median employees, Jassy's ratio was exceptionally high, sparking controversy among shareholder advisory firms.

title: Amazon consumer CEO Dave Clark resigns
summary: Dave Clark, Amazon's consumer CEO, has resigned after 23 years with the company, effective July 1. His departure signals potential changes in the consumer division, which faced challenges with overbuilt warehouse space and a weak profit outlook. CEO Andy Jassy acknowledged the need for further improvements and will announce a succession plan in the coming weeks.

title: Investing in Big Data with Data Center REITs
summary: This article explores the concept of investing in data center Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) as a way to gain exposure to the big data sector. While acknowledging the appeal of REITs for diversification and income, the authors argue that data center REITs carry significant risks, resembling tech stocks more than traditional real estate investments. They conclude that such REITs offer too much risk without sufficient upside potential, suggesting alternative investments like NVIDIA for data center growth exposure.

title: Get a TCL Roku Smart TV for $100 during Walmart+ Weekend
summary: Walmart+ Weekend is offering a 32-inch TCL Roku Smart TV for just $100. This budget-friendly TV includes features like 720p HD resolution, access to numerous streaming services via Roku, voice control, and an ARC HDMI port, making it a solid deal for those looking for an affordable smart TV. The deal is available until June 5th for Walmart+ members.

title: What Does Amazon's Stock Split Mean for Investors?
summary: Amazon is executing a 20-1 stock split, its first in over two decades, effective June 3. The split will adjust Morningstar's fair value estimate for Amazon to $192 per share from $3,850, but senior analyst Dan Romanoff's long-term view remains unchanged, anticipating continued growth in e-commerce, AWS, and advertising. Other major tech companies like Alphabet and Tesla are also planning stock splits.

title: Teresa Carlson returns to Microsoft
summary: Teresa Carlson has rejoined Microsoft as a corporate Vice President and executive-in-residence, nearly 12 years after her previous departure. Carlson, a prominent figure in government cloud computing, left Amazon Web Services where she led their public sector growth, and then had a brief stint as chief growth officer at Splunk before her recent move back to Microsoft. Her return marks a significant development in her career trajectory within the technology industry.

title: Amazon executive behind its massive delivery operation to leave after 23 years
summary: Dave Clark, the Amazon executive responsible for building its vast delivery network, is stepping down as CEO of the company's consumer business after 23 years. His departure signifies a shift in Amazon's leadership following Jeff Bezos's exit and comes as the company faces economic challenges, including a recent $2 billion hit from overbuilt warehousing and transportation capacity. Clark, known for taking risks like acquiring planes and championing warehouse robots, indicated he wants to return to "building" and leaves Amazon with a plan to address inflationary challenges.

title: Ford Motor Company Will Start Online, Fixed-Price, No Haggle Sales For EVs (Updated with Video!)
summary: Ford CEO Jim Farley announced that the company will transition to 100% online, fixed-price sales for its electric vehicles, including direct delivery to customers' homes. This move aims to bypass the traditional dealership experience and excessive markups, following a model similar to Tesla and drawing inspiration from companies like Target and Amazon. While dealerships will still exist, they will need to adapt to this new online-focused, no-haggle sales approach for EVs, with potential expansion to all vehicle sales if successful.

title: Toxic Products Sold at Dollar Stores
summary: A report by the Campaign for Healthier Solutions reveals that over half of products tested from dollar stores like Family Dollar, Dollar General, and Five Below contain hazardous chemicals. These toxic products, some targeted at children, include substances like lead, phthalates, PVC, BPAs, and PFAS, which are linked to various health issues. The article lists 30 specific toxic products found in dollar stores, ranging from children's headphones and toys to food packaging and cooking pans.

title: Edgewell Personal Care Announces Gen-Z Focused Clean Skincare Brand
summary: Edgewell Personal Care has launched Fieldtrip, a new unisex clean skincare brand aimed at Gen-Z consumers. The brand emphasizes ethically sourced natural ingredients, sustainable packaging, and a commitment to social responsibility through a partnership with Keep America Beautiful’s RETREET program. Fieldtrip offers an initial lineup of seven products, available online and expanding to retailers like Nordstrom and Macy's in August, with more products slated for release in Fall 2022.

title: Teladoc hit with class-action suit alleging it misled investors
summary: Teladoc is facing a new class-action lawsuit alleging that the company, along with its CEO and CFO, knowingly misled investors about its business prospects and downplayed competition. This suit follows a significant drop in Teladoc's stock price after the virtual care company missed revenue expectations and reported a $6.6 billion impairment charge related to its Livongo acquisition in its first-quarter results. The lawsuit claims investors bought shares at "artificially inflated prices" and suffered substantial losses, though Teladoc has called the litigation "frivolous."

title: Amazon (AMZN) Gains as Stock Split Lowers Price Tag for Retail Buyers
summary: Amazon's stock surged after a 20-for-1 split, making shares more accessible to retail investors. This marks the company's first split in over two decades, leading to increased trading volume and outperforming the Nasdaq 100 Index. The move is expected to attract greater retail interest, potentially acting as a sentiment catalyst.

title: Peloton Appoints Liz Coddington as Chief Financial Officer
summary: Peloton Interactive, Inc. announced the appointment of Liz Coddington as its new Chief Financial Officer, effective June 13, 2022. Ms. Coddington brings over two decades of financial experience from companies like Amazon Web Services, Walmart.com, and Netflix. She succeeds Jill Woodworth, who will transition to a consultant role to ensure a smooth handover and support the reporting of FY2022 financial results.

title: Netflix Gearing Up for Formula 1 Rights Push
summary: Netflix is reportedly vying for the U.S. broadcast rights to Formula 1, marking its first potential move into live sports. The streaming giant is competing with ESPN, Amazon, and NBCUniversal for the rights, which are sought at around $100 million annually by F1's parent company, Liberty Media. This interest comes as F1's popularity in the U.S. has surged, partly due to Netflix's "Drive to Survive" docuseries, and coincides with Netflix's plans to introduce an ad-supported tier.

title: U.S. Supreme Court rules Southwest Airlines cannot force wage suit into arbitration
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled 8-0 that Southwest Airlines cannot force a baggage handler's class action lawsuit over overtime pay into private arbitration, exempting them from a federal law due to their involvement in interstate commerce. This decision has potential implications for other companies like Amazon and Uber, as it suggests that various transportation workers may also be exempt from mandatory arbitration for wage claims, leading to more class actions rather than individual arbitrations.

title: XPO Logistics Appoints Yoav Amiel as Chief Information Officer
summary: XPO Logistics has appointed Yoav Amiel as Chief Information Officer for its planned spin-off of the asset-light brokered transportation platform. Amiel, who previously led the technology organization for XPO’s North American transportation division, has been critical in developing the XPO Connect digital brokerage platform. This move supports the spin-off's creation of two separate, publicly traded companies focused on North American growth.

title: With shares of Kansas City’s Cerner turned over, sale to Oracle will close Wednesday
summary: Oracle's acquisition of Cerner Corporation for $28.3 billion is set to formally close on Wednesday, June 8th, following a successful stock tender offer. This acquisition marks Oracle's largest ever and signifies its entry into the healthcare market, with Cerner continuing as a dedicated subsidiary and Oracle pledging to grow jobs in Kansas City. The deal concludes Cerner's status as the largest private employer under local control in Kansas City, a company founded in 1979.

title: Oracle closes $28B deal to buy EHR giant Cerner
summary: Oracle has finalized its $28.3 billion acquisition of health IT company Cerner, marking its largest acquisition to date and a significant move to expand into the healthcare market. The deal, which involved Oracle finalizing a stock tender offer with 69.2% of Cerner shares, aims to leverage Cerner as an "anchor asset" to scale Oracle's cloud business in hospitals and health systems. This acquisition positions Oracle to transform healthcare delivery through new information systems and addresses the growing trend of big tech companies investing heavily in the healthcare IT sector.

title: Teladoc Health faces class action lawsuit alleging it misled investors
summary: Teladoc Health is facing a class action lawsuit alleging the company, its CEO Jason Gorevic, and CFO Mala Murthy misled investors. The suit claims they failed to disclose that increasing competition was negatively impacting its BetterHelp mental health and chronic care segments, leading to unsustainable growth projections. This alleged misrepresentation resulted in significant investor losses and a $6.6 billion non-cash goodwill impairment charge related to its 2020 Livongo acquisition.

title: Kohl’s Corp. negotiating company sale to owner of The Vitamin Shoppe
summary: Kohl’s Corp. has entered into exclusive negotiations with Franchise Group, Inc., owner of The Vitamin Shoppe, regarding a potential acquisition at $60 per share. This development comes amid ongoing shareholder pressure and previous attempts to acquire the company. While the deal’s certainty is unknown, an expert noted the buyer might see an undervalued asset rather than bringing strategic advantages to Kohl's.

title: Amazon Sued Over 'Bait-And-Switch' Whole Foods Fee
summary: Amazon is facing a putative class action lawsuit filed by an Amazon Prime member in Washington federal court. The lawsuit alleges that Amazon engaged in "bait-and-switch" false advertising by promising free grocery services for Whole Foods Market orders but then added a $9.95 service fee. The plaintiff claims this practice constitutes false advertising.

title: Mississippi REIT gets chunk of SF industrial market
summary: EastGroup Properties, a Mississippi-based REIT, acquired Tulloch Corp. in Oakland for approximately $415 million, gaining 14 industrial properties totaling 1.7 million square feet, predominantly in the San Francisco Bay Area. This acquisition significantly boosts EastGroup's California portfolio, increasing its holdings to 7.6 million square feet. Despite recent market shifts, EastGroup remains optimistic about the Bay Area industrial market due to strong tenant demand.

title: Etsy sellers getting squeezed by ‘Amazon effect’
summary: Etsy sellers are facing increasing pressure due to rising fees, consumer expectations for fast and free shipping, and competition from larger platforms like Amazon, leading to shrinking profit margins. The article highlights the experiences of sellers who participated in a strike, dealt with copyright infringement issues, and are considering moving to alternative platforms like Shopify to regain control over their businesses and artistic integrity. This "Amazon effect" is forcing many small business owners to adapt or seek new avenues to sell their handmade products.

title: Amazon’s former No. 2 Dave Clark just joined a Bay Area logistics startup as co-CEO
summary: Dave Clark, formerly Amazon's consumer chief, has joined Flexport Inc. as co-CEO. He will serve in this role for six months starting September 1st, after which he will become the sole CEO, with current CEO Ryan Petersen transitioning to executive chairman. Clark's departure from Amazon comes amidst slowing online sales growth and an excess of warehouse space, concluding a two-decade career where he championed innovation in Amazon's fulfillment and transportation sectors.

title: Ex-Amazon worker accused of stealing personal data of 100M Capital One customers goes on trial
summary: A former Amazon software engineer, Paige Thompson, is on trial for allegedly stealing personal data from over 100 million Capital One customers in one of the largest data breaches in US history. Prosecutors claim she intended to commit identity theft and profit, while her defense argues she was acting as a "white-hat hacker" trying to expose vulnerabilities in the bank's system. Thompson faces 10 counts of computer fraud, wire fraud, and identity theft, and if convicted, could face up to 30 years in prison.

title: Stellantis Stock Is Undervalued, Even as It Catches Up in the Electric Vehicle Market
summary: Stellantis, formed from the 2021 merger of Fiat Chrysler and Peugeot, is making an aggressive push into the electric vehicle market after being a laggard. Despite its efforts to catch up, Morningstar analysts consider Stellantis stock undervalued, trading at a significant discount to its peers. The company plans an all-electric lineup for its luxury brands by 2024 and aims for 50% EV sales in North America by 2030, alongside ambitious carbon reduction and revenue growth targets.

title: Kroger is now delivering in South Florida
summary: Kroger has launched online grocery delivery services in South Florida through a new 60,000-square-foot spoke facility in Miami, which supports its automated customer fulfillment center in Groveland, Florida. This expansion is part of Kroger's aggressive growth strategy in Florida, utilizing a hub-and-spoke network to deliver groceries to areas hundreds of miles from its CFCs. The company aims to compete with rivals like Amazon and Walmart by focusing on next-day delivery, a wide assortment, competitive pricing, and its partnership with Ocado, particularly in markets where it lacks physical stores.

title: Dow dives 800 points, S&P 500 posts worst week since January after inflation hits 40-year high
summary: U.S. stocks fell sharply on Friday, with the Dow dropping 880 points and the S&P 500 completing its worst week since January, following a higher-than-expected inflation report for May. The consumer price index reached its highest level since 1981, showing an 8.6% year-over-year increase, fueling concerns about a potential recession and prompting fears of a more aggressive Federal Reserve. Tech stocks, banks, and cyclical stocks were particularly impacted as the 2-year Treasury yield surged above 3%.

title: Fortinet (FTNT) to Split Stock in 5 to Attract More Investors
summary: Fortinet (FTNT) announced a five-for-one forward stock split, effective June 22, aiming to make its shares more accessible to employees and retail investors. This move is expected to boost demand and further increase share prices, building on its impressive 710% return over the past five years. Other tech giants like Alphabet, Amazon, and NVIDIA have also recently undertaken stock splits for similar reasons.

title: Hack Into Quantum Computing Boom With QQQ
summary: Quantum computing, a disruptive technology with significant growth potential, is still in its early stages but offers various use cases. While some speculative companies exist, major players in this field are large-cap companies. The Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) and Invesco NASDAQ 100 ETF (QQQM) provide investors with exposure to quantum computing through their holdings in established tech giants like Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Nvidia, and Honeywell.

title: Fortinet (FTNT) to Split Stock in 5 to Attract More Investors
summary: Fortinet (FTNT) announced a five-for-one forward stock split to make its shares more accessible to employees and retail investors, with stockholder approval scheduled for June 17. If approved, the stock price will drop from approximately $300 to $60 per share. This move follows similar stock splits by other major tech companies like Alphabet, Amazon, and NVIDIA, aiming to boost demand and potentially increase share prices.

title: Lululemon leases an additional 120K square feet of office space
summary: Lululemon Athletica Inc. has signed one of Vancouver's largest office lease deals since 2018, securing an additional 120,000 square feet across nine floors at Burrard Place. This transaction signals a strong commitment to office space by large firms, challenging the pandemic-driven narrative of reduced office demand. The new space is located near Lululemon's current headquarters and is scheduled for occupancy in late 2022.

title: Walmart struggles to solve consumer needs in China
summary: Walmart has faced persistent challenges in the Chinese market since opening its first store in 1996, struggling to compete with local retailers known for their diverse product offerings and fast home deliveries. The company's large hypermarket format is not appealing to Chinese consumers who prefer online shopping and local products. Additionally, Walmart has found itself navigating complex political tensions, including controversies over product sourcing from Xinjiang and increased regulatory scrutiny, despite China being crucial for its manufacturing supply chain and for observing e-commerce trends.

title: Oracle’s Database Dominance Eroded by Rise of Cloud-First Rivals
summary: Oracle's long-standing dominance in the database market is being challenged by cloud-first rivals offering more flexible and cheaper options. Companies like Shutterfly are migrating their data to cloud providers such as Amazon.com Inc., moving away from Oracle's traditional database products due to ease of use. Despite this trend, Oracle is still projected to report 4% sales growth.

title: Judge Dismisses Class Action Lawsuit Filed Against GoodRx
summary: A federal judge has dismissed a class action lawsuit filed against GoodRx Holdings, Inc. The lawsuit alleged that GoodRx made misleading statements and filed a misleading registration statement and prospectus regarding its initial public offering, particularly concerning the competitive threat posed by Amazon. The judge ruled that the plaintiffs failed to sufficiently plead facts establishing falsity, concrete knowledge by GoodRx of Amazon's plans, or scienter.

title: System Report: American Eagle Outfitters embraces fulfillment at the edge
summary: American Eagle Outfitters (AEO) is innovating its fulfillment strategy, moving beyond traditional distribution centers to embrace "fulfillment at the edge" to meet soaring e-commerce demands and customer expectations for speed. By acquiring Quiet Logistics and AirTerra, AEO is strategically positioning inventory closer to major metropolitan areas using a network of smaller fulfillment centers that leverage autonomous mobile robots and advanced software. This new approach, developed under Shekar Natarajan, aims to enhance efficiency, reduce delivery times, and potentially create a shared supply chain model with other retailers.

title: Amazon Prime Air prepares for drone deliveries
summary: Amazon's Prime Air drone delivery service is preparing to launch in Lockeford, California, marking a significant step in making drone deliveries a reality after nearly a decade of development. The service aims to deliver packages quickly and safely, leveraging advanced sense-and-avoid technology to navigate obstacles and ensure safe landings without human observers. Lockeford residents will provide crucial feedback to help scale the service, which has earned an FAA air carrier certificate through rigorous testing and innovation.

title: Semiconductor giant Marvell plans ‘significant expansion’ of Kanata footprint after acquisition
summary: Marvell, a U.S. semiconductor company, is significantly expanding its presence in Canada, particularly in Kanata, following its acquisition of local microchip design firms. The company plans to build out its offices in Ottawa, Toronto, and Vancouver to develop semiconductor technology for cloud, 5G, and automotive markets. Marvell expects to leverage Ottawa's tech talent and academic partnerships for its growth, with a focus on cutting-edge technologies.

title: Grassroots mojo and 4 other reasons Starbucks workers have been so successful unionizing
summary: Starbucks Workers United has achieved significant success in unionizing stores across the U.S., winning over 100 elections since December 2021. This unexpected success is attributed to a shift in public sentiment towards unions, a replicable worker-driven organizing model, Starbucks' progressive brand attracting pro-union employees, a strong sense of community among baristas, and a decentralized, grassroots approach to organizing. This movement could signal a broader union revival in the service sector.

title: Stipends for remote work emerge as polarizing issue
summary: The rise of permanent remote work has sparked debate over whether companies should reimburse employees for home office expenses like internet and electricity, especially if remote work is by choice. This issue presents legal implications, with some states requiring reimbursement, and has led to lawsuits, such as one against Amazon in California. Experts suggest that while legal obligations vary, decisions around reimbursement will also influence employee morale and experience.

title: Steve Rendle’s Pay at VF Tops $15 Million
summary: VF Corp. CEO Steve Rendle received $15.4 million in total compensation last year, a 2.3% decrease from the previous year. The majority of his compensation, $10.3 million, was in stock and option awards, tying his pay to shareholder performance. Rendle is navigating challenges like inflation and supply chain issues for VF's diverse brand portfolio, which includes Supreme, Vans, and The North Face.

title: Edgewell debuts Gen Z-focused skincare brand, Fieldtrip
summary: Edgewell has launched Fieldtrip, a new clean skincare brand aimed at Gen Z consumers. The brand offers unisex products with luxury formulations under $25, initially sold direct-to-consumer and on Amazon, with plans to expand to Nordstrom and Macy's. Fieldtrip emphasizes sustainability and affordability, aligning with Gen Z's values.

title: Drones will start delivering Amazon packages this year, company says
summary: Amazon announced that it will begin delivering packages via its Prime Air drone service to residents in Lockeford, California, later this year. The company has spent nearly a decade developing its drone technology, which includes a sophisticated sense-and-avoid system to ensure safe operation. Amazon is working with the FAA and local officials to implement the service and plans to invest in the Lockeford community.

title: Lululemon Goes Back to Work in Style with Massive New Vancouver Office
summary: Lululemon Athletica Inc. is significantly expanding its real estate footprint in its hometown of Vancouver by leasing close to 120,000 sq. ft of office space in the new Burrard Place building. This deal is considered one of the largest office lease transactions in downtown Vancouver since the pandemic, signaling a commitment by large firms to office spaces despite ongoing debates about remote and hybrid work models. The expansion comes as Lululemon also makes headlines for other real estate ventures and new product releases.

title: Newmark Completes Sale of Moffett Green, Fully-Leased Trophy Campus in Silicon Valley
summary: Newmark has successfully completed the sale of Moffett Green, a 719,037 square-foot, fully-leased trophy office campus in Sunnyvale, California, to CommonWealth Partners, LLC. The transaction, which represents the largest single-asset investment office sale in Silicon Valley history, involved Meta Platforms, Inc. as the long-term tenant. Steven Golubchik and his team at Newmark facilitated the deal, highlighting continued investor demand for prime assets in high-barrier-to-entry markets and the strong performance of Moffett Park.

title: Next-Generation Adobe Analytics Delivers Customer Insights From Streaming Media and the Metaverse
summary: Adobe has launched new services for Adobe Analytics, creating a unified workspace for brands to gather data and insights from various media, including the metaverse and streaming content. This update allows for seamless data migration from other analytics platforms, ensuring compliance with regulations like GDPR and CCPA. By supporting emerging channels, Adobe Analytics aims to provide comprehensive omnichannel analysis through Customer Journey Analytics, helping businesses understand evolving consumer behaviors and deliver personalized experiences.

title: eBay Inc. stock falls Tuesday, underperforms market
summary: eBay Inc. (EBAY) stock dropped 0.82% to $42.58 on Tuesday, underperforming the broader market as the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also saw declines. This marked the fourth consecutive day of losses for eBay, with the stock closing significantly below its 52-week high. Competitors showed mixed performance, with Amazon.com Inc. falling, while Walmart Inc. and Costco Wholesale Corp. rose.

title: The Surprising Case for Stronger E-commerce Growth
summary: Despite a recent slump in e-commerce stocks and slowing economic activity, Morgan Stanley forecasts continued strong growth for e-commerce, projecting an increase from $3.3 trillion today to $5.4 trillion in 2026. This growth is driven by a permanent behavioral shift to online shopping, increasing penetration in both developed and emerging markets, and technological improvements in logistics and digital payments.

title: Everything You Wanted to Know About Bear Markets
summary: This article discusses the characteristics of bear markets, noting that while bull markets are similar, bear markets each have unique causes. Author Frank Holmes explains that the current bear market is due to pandemic-related liquidity, rampant inflation, and aggressive central bank actions, including a recent significant interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve. He advises investors to stay diversified, consider adding gold to their portfolios, and maintain a positive outlook given that bear markets are typically short-lived and can present buying opportunities.

title: Meet Naima Greenwood | President & Chief Operating Officer, Yardstick Management
summary: The article features an interview with Naima Greenwood, President & Chief Operating Officer of Yardstick Management, the nation's leading Black-owned management consulting firm. Greenwood discusses the firm's significant impact on diversity, equity, and inclusion within global organizations like Amazon and Netflix, and their commitment to leveling the playing field for marginalized communities. She also shares personal insights about Atlanta, where Yardstick Management is headquartered, and highlights the important community work of the Villages of Carver YMCA.

title: Sonos tips: how to stereo pair, connect to a TV, and more
summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide to getting the most out of a Sonos system, covering frequently asked questions and offering 25 tips and tricks. It details aspects like Bluetooth connectivity, using Sonos without Wi-Fi, connecting to a TV, app usage, waterproofing, stereo pairing, and enhancing sound quality with Trueplay and external DACs. The guide also touches on streaming services, voice control, and integrating vinyl with Sonos, demonstrating the system's versatility.

title: How to cancel Amazon Prime: Here's how to end your membership in a few steps
summary: This article provides a simple, three-step guide on how to cancel an Amazon Prime membership. It details logging into Amazon, navigating to the Prime account settings, and selecting the "End membership" option. The piece also notes that benefits will continue until the end of the current billing cycle.

title: hololive production Announces New Apparel Sales on Merch by Amazon
summary: hololive production has announced a new line of apparel featuring various talents, which will be available globally via Merch by Amazon starting June 16, 2022. The white T-shirts depict talents like Tokino Sora, Robocosan, and Hoshimachi Suisei, and are shippable to customers in France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Spain, the United Kingdom, and the United States. Merch by Amazon handles production, sales, and shipping of these creator-designed products, offering standard Amazon shipping options.

title: Instead of IPL, Amazon wants to spend money building e-com biz
summary: Amazon has decided against bidding for media rights to the Indian Premier League, opting instead to invest billions into its e-commerce business in India. The company, led by Manish Tiwary, aims to expand its reach beyond major cities to non-English speaking, less affluent populations in rural areas, targeting an additional 100 million shoppers. This strategy involves initiatives like "Smart Commerce" to digitize small merchants and using local influencers.

title: Amazon Prime announces 2022 Prime Day dates will be held on July 12, 13
summary: Amazon announced that its 2022 Prime Day sales event will take place on July 12 and 13. The 48-hour event, starting at 3 AM ET, will offer discounts across various categories and include Poland and Sweden for the first time. The annual event aims to boost Prime subscriptions and generate significant sales, impacting rival retailers who often hold their own sales concurrently.

title: Canada's Telus strikes C$2.9 bln deal for LifeWorks in healthcare push
summary: Canadian wireless carrier Telus Corp is acquiring LifeWorks Inc for C$2.9 billion, aiming to leverage the increasing demand for mental health services from employers, a trend exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic. The deal will combine LifeWorks with Telus Health, expanding its virtual healthcare offerings and aiming for annual savings of C$170 million to C$200 million over the next three to five years, including a significant presence in the U.S.

title: The Big Interview: Expedia Group CTO Rathi Murthy
summary: Expedia Group CTO Rathi Murthy discusses the company's "Expedia Open World" vision, a new API-centric, modular travel platform designed to allow more flexible integration for partners. She details the challenges of this large-scale transformation while the company is actively operating, emphasizing a "people, process, technology" approach and an iterative, accountability-driven methodology. The article highlights Expedia's move to AWS and their focus on hiring diverse talent.

title: Bluepeak rebrands from Vast Broadband, expanding internet in Sioux Falls
summary: Vast Broadband, a Sioux Falls internet provider, has rebranded as Bluepeak to reflect its expansion efforts in Sioux Falls and other states. The company plans to build fiber-optic cables to improve service reliability and internet speed for both existing and future customers. Bluepeak currently serves about 8,000 people in Sioux Falls and anticipates construction to continue expanding northward through summer 2023.

title: Dick’s Sporting Goods Expanding, Burlington Moving to Town Square
summary: Dick's Sporting Goods is set to expand significantly in the Town Square Mall, taking over the neighboring Dollar Tree space. Additionally, Burlington is relocating its store from the Oakdale Mall in Johnson City to the Town Square Mall, occupying the former A.C. Moore Arts & Crafts location, with construction already underway.

title: Ariana Grande Debuts Chapter 3 of R.E.M. Beauty with a Bang(s)
summary: Ariana Grande's R.E.M. Beauty launched its third collection, 'Chapter 3: on your collar,' focusing on lip products. This collection, which includes five new formulas like lip oil, balm, liner, and lipsticks, follows the brand's 'drops' model and continues its extraterrestrial aesthetic. R.E.M. Beauty's initial collections, Chapters 1 and 2, are also available at Ulta stores.

title: Former Amazon employee convicted in Capital One hack
summary: A former Amazon Web Services employee, Paige Thompson, has been convicted of hacking into Capital One and stealing the data of over 100 million people, making it one of the largest data breaches in the U.S. Thompson was found guilty of seven federal crimes, including wire fraud, and her sentencing is set for September 15. Capital One has previously agreed to pay $190 million to settle a class-action lawsuit and an additional $80 million in regulatory fines related to the breach.

title: Ex-Amazon employee convicted over 2019 Capital One breach
summary: A former Amazon Web Services (AWS) employee, Paige Thompson, has been convicted of seven federal crimes related to the 2019 Capital One data breach that affected over 106 million accounts. The breach led to Capital One paying an $80 million penalty and a $190 million settlement for customer lawsuits. Thompson, who is scheduled for sentencing in September, exploited misconfigured AWS accounts to steal personal data and mine cryptocurrency.

title: False Advertising Lawsuit Against Vital Farms Wins Right to Proceed
summary: PETA Foundation lawyers and co-counsel achieved a legal victory as a motion to dismiss a class-action lawsuit against Vital Farms Inc. was denied. This decision allows the case to proceed, brought by consumers alleging they were misled by the company's false claims of ethical and humane treatment of hens. Vital Farms' eggs are widely sold at major grocery chains.

title: Digital Pharmacy Market Growth, Drivers, and Opportunities
summary: The global digital pharmacy market is projected to grow significantly from USD 96.5 billion in 2022 to USD 211.9 billion by 2027, driven by factors such as increasing consumer preference for online medicine purchases, especially post-COVID-19, market consolidations, and an aging population. North America currently holds the largest market share, while emerging markets like China and India present substantial opportunities. Key challenges include the presence of illegal pharmacies and the lack of comprehensive regulatory frameworks worldwide.

title: Paige Thompson found guilty in 2019 Capital One data breach
summary: Paige Thompson, a former Amazon engineer, has been convicted in the 2019 Capital One data breach that exposed data of over 100 million customers. The hack involved misconfigured AWS accounts and cost Capital One hundreds of millions in fines and settlements. Thompson was found guilty of wire fraud and multiple counts of unauthorized access to a protected computer and damaging a protected computer, though acquitted on other charges.

title: Former AWS engineer convicted over hack that cost Capital One $270m
summary: A former AWS engineer, Paige Thompson, has been convicted of seven counts of fraud for stealing personal data from over 100 million people, including Capital One customers, after identifying and exploiting misconfigured AWS accounts. The breach has cost Capital One more than $270 million in compensation and regulatory fines. Thompson, who also used the breached accounts for cryptojacking, is awaiting sentencing in September.

title: Corsair Dark Core RGB Pro SE wireless gaming mouse review
summary: The Corsair Dark Core RGB Pro SE is a heavy, feature-rich wireless gaming mouse offering excellent connectivity and ergonomics. While praised for its build quality, customizable RGB, and precise sensor, its significant weight (142g) and mediocre battery life (20 hours with RGB on) are notable drawbacks, especially for competitive FPS players. The review concludes that it's a great option for those who prefer comfortable, heavier mice for productivity and slower-paced games, rather than twitch shooters.

title: First Watch Adds Bumble Executive Stephanie Lilak to Board of Directors
summary: First Watch Restaurant Group has appointed Stephanie Lilak, Chief People Officer of Bumble Inc., to its Board of Directors, effective June 17, 2022. Lilak will join the Audit Committee and Compensation Committee, bringing extensive human resources experience from her roles at Bumble Inc., Dunkin’ Brands, and General Mills. Her appointment is expected to support First Watch’s growth and its people-centric "You First" culture.

title: Oracle introduces lower-cost version of its full on-premises cloud stack
summary: Oracle has introduced a more affordable version of its on-premises cloud stack, Dedicated Region Cloud@Customer, alongside a new rack-level offering called Oracle Compute Cloud@Customer. The new Dedicated Region Cloud@Customer reduces the required space and annual cost significantly, making Oracle's full public cloud services, including Fusion applications, accessible to a broader range of global companies for workloads that cannot fully migrate to the public cloud. Oracle Compute Cloud@Customer provides managed on-site computing and storage resources for smaller workloads, similar to offerings from AWS, Microsoft, and Google.

title: Build a data pipeline on AWS with Kafka, Kafka connect and DynamoDB
summary: This article provides a step-by-step guide to building a data pipeline on AWS using Kafka, Kafka Connect, and DynamoDB. It covers setting up MSK, MSK Connect, and integrating Datagen source connector with a DynamoDB sink connector. The guide also details infrastructure preparation using CloudFormation and testing the end-to-end pipeline.

title: Virtual reality and indoor ‘tree houses’: Truist unveils banking tech center in uptown
summary: Truist Bank has opened a new 100,000-square-foot Innovation and Technology Center in uptown Charlotte, aiming to fuse tech and finance for a better banking experience. The center features virtual reality labs, "tree houses," and collaborative spaces, intending to propel Truist into the future of digital banking despite recent low rankings in consumer satisfaction for its digital services. The bank also launched an "Innovators in Residence" program with partners like Verizon and Amazon Web Services to explore new technologies.

title: Barack, Michelle Obama ditch Spotify for Amazon-owned Audible
summary: Former President Barack Obama and former First Lady Michelle Obama are moving their podcast content from Spotify to Amazon-owned Audible. Their production company, Higher Ground, will create new audio content for Audible, a platform primarily known for audiobooks. The Obamas cited Audible's investment in lifting up voices and telling stories that entertain and inspire as reasons for the switch.

title: MinIO extends Snowflake analysis to any data location
summary: MinIO has partnered with Snowflake to enable Snowflake analytics on data stored in any location, not just within Snowflake's own environment. This partnership allows customers to leverage external table support in MinIO for cost-effective analysis of large datasets without moving them to the cloud. This provides flexibility similar to recent Snowflake partnerships with Dell and Pure Storage, offering various options for on-premises or cloud-based data analysis.

title: Dickies is turning 100 years old. It’s gone viral with Gen Z
summary: Dickies, the utilitarian workwear brand, is celebrating its 100th anniversary and has unexpectedly gone viral with Gen Z, particularly with its 874 trousers. This surge in popularity is attributed to a combination of celebrity dressing, collaborations, product seeding to Depop sellers, and organic TikTok trends, where young people are styling the affordably priced trousers in creative ways. The brand has capitalized on this by resharing user-generated content, launching new styles, and enabling affiliate marketing through platforms like Amazon, demonstrating how authentic connection with subcultures and accessibility can drive significant engagement among a new generation.

title: Zscaler and AWS Expand Relationship
summary: Zscaler and Amazon Web Services (AWS) have extended their partnership to provide unified cloud security solutions built on Zscaler’s Zero Trust architecture. These innovations aim to simplify cloud security operations, accelerate cloud adoption, and protect cloud workloads and 5G connections. The collaboration delivers a new Posture Control™ solution built on AWS, extends Zero Trust security to AWS workloads, and enables Zero Trust for private 5G using AWS Wavelength.

title: Best Buy has Motorola's MA1 adapter back in stock, so grab it while you can
summary: The Motorola MA1 wireless Android Auto adapter is currently back in stock at Best Buy, after frequently selling out quickly due to high demand. The adapter, which allows for wireless Android Auto connectivity, has garnered positive user reviews and is a popular item, making its availability at Best Buy a notable event for those seeking the sought-after device.

title: Avnet, and Amazon Web Services enters into a global strategic partnership
summary: Avnet and Amazon Web Services (AWS) have formed a global strategic partnership aimed at helping Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) of IoT solutions accelerate their time to market. This collaboration will enable Avnet’s IoTConnect Platform to leverage AWS's extensive portfolio of services, creating a scalable and secure platform for application-specific usage. The partnership provides OEMs with pre-integrated and abstracted capabilities, such as device provisioning, multi-layer security, and business intelligence, allowing them to focus on differentiating their connected products.

summary: ODP Corp., the owner of Office Depot and OfficeMax, has decided to remain a

title: Despite Shopify’s Stock Split, Investors Should Look Elsewhere
summary: Morningstar analyst Sandy Ward advises investors to look beyond Shopify's stock split, suggesting Amazon shares as a better alternative. Shopify's stock has plummeted significantly, and concerns about its financial outlook and a new share class cementing founder control make it a less attractive investment compared to Amazon, which offers greater financial certainty and diversified revenue streams. Despite a potential upside, Shopify is not among Morningstar's top stock picks due to slowing revenue growth and quarterly losses.

title: Amazon has a plan to make Alexa mimic anyone's voice
summary: Amazon is developing a new Alexa feature that will allow the voice assistant to mimic any voice after hearing less than a minute of audio. The company's senior vice president, Rohit Prasad, stated the goal is to "make the memories last" for those who have lost loved ones, particularly after the pandemic. This technology, however, raises concerns about its potential for abuse, such as creating deepfakes, an issue Microsoft has also addressed with its voice-parroting software.

title: Here’s how much the Jif peanut butter recall could cost parent company JM Smucker
summary: The J.M. Smucker Company could face a $125 million impact from the massive recall of nearly 50 Jif peanut butter products due to a salmonella outbreak. The recall, originating from the company's Lexington plant, led to a 15% drop in stock price. Production has resumed, and products are expected back on shelves shortly, with heightened food safety measures in place.

title: Chinese DPU chip firm gains funds, unicorn status ...
summary: Jaguar Microsystems, a Chinese Data Processing Unit (DPU) chip company founded in 2020 by former Broadcom executive Sunny Siu, has secured hundreds of millions of yuan in funding, propelling its valuation to unicorn status at approximately US$1.34 billion. The financing round was led by Tencent Holdings Ltd. and included other major investors. Jaguar Microsystems, which employs nearly 400 staff, released an FPGA version of its DPU in 2021 and plans for mass production of its system-chip version by 2023, primarily targeting cloud computing and internet companies, with Tencent expected to be a key customer.

title: Por qué un empresario propone colocar "estatuas de Cristina Kirchner en cada rincón de Uruguay"
summary: A Brazilian venture capitalist, Paulo Passoni, has provocatively suggested erecting statues of Cristina Kirchner across Uruguay. He argues that her policies have inadvertently driven a significant number of Argentine entrepreneurs and tech companies to relocate to Uruguay, appreciating its stable economic environment and clear rules. This migration has fostered a thriving tech ecosystem in Uruguay, benefiting the country by attracting talent and investment.

title: JPMorgan Chase Joins Companies Paying Employees Who Travel for Abortions
summary: JPMorgan Chase announced it would cover travel expenses for employees needing to travel out of state for abortions, expanding a benefit that covers services unavailable near an employee's home. This decision follows the Supreme Court's overturning of Roe v. Wade and aligns JPMorgan with other companies like Citigroup, Starbucks, Amazon, Tesla, and Yelp making similar pledges. The move addresses the implications of state-level abortion bans, with many states poised to restrict or ban abortions following the ruling.

title: Seattle Pride’s Biggest Sponsors Also Give Big to Homophobic Politicians
summary: This article exposes how major corporate sponsors of Seattle Pride, specifically Alaska Air Group, Chateau Ste. Michelle, and T-Mobile, also donate significant amounts of money to politicians who oppose LGBTQ+ rights. It details specific examples of these donations and the voting records of the politicians supported. The article questions the alignment of these corporations' actions with Pride values and notes that Seattle Pride is reviewing its corporate partnerships.

title: Omnicom banks on Walmart, Instacart in latest commerce expansion
summary: Omnicom Media Group (OMG) has expanded its commerce offerings by partnering with Walmart Connect and Instacart. The Walmart partnership focuses on cross-screen planning and connecting first-party advertiser data to Walmart's DSP, while the Instacart collaboration includes account management, product insights, and utilizing Omni's clean room infrastructure. These moves aim to deepen Omnicom's connected commerce capabilities and help advertisers navigate a privacy-centric marketing landscape.

title: 3 Reasons to Buy TJX Companies, and 1 to Sell
summary: TJX Companies, the parent company of TJ Maxx and Marshalls, is highlighted as a resilient brick-and-mortar retailer with an evergreen business model benefitting from the "retail apocalypse" and offering deeply discounted goods. The article outlines three reasons to buy the stock: its solid business model, robust post-lockdown recovery, and attractive valuation coupled with a decent dividend. The primary reason to sell is potential macroeconomic headwinds such as inflation, higher freight costs, and supply chain disruptions, which could impact its margins and inventory management.

title: Private Prisons Are a Socially Responsible Investment, According to Bizarre Wall Street Measures
summary: This article critiques the Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) investing framework, particularly highlighting how private prison company CoreCivic leveraged a "racial equity audit" to improve its public image and attract investment despite its controversial practices. It argues that ESG funds often engage in "greenwashing" and "socialwashing," allowing companies with questionable core business models to appear socially responsible through superficial metrics like diversity quotas, while critics assert that these measures enrich consultants and fund managers without achieving real social impact. The article further exposes the inconsistencies and lack of regulation in ESG rankings, showing how companies like Exxon Mobil and McDonald's can receive favorable ESG scores despite contributing to environmental or social problems, and how many ESG funds have higher fees than traditional index funds with similar holdings.

title: CVS, Rite Aid ration contraceptive pills as demand surges
summary: CVS Health Corp. and Rite Aid Corp. are limiting purchases of emergency contraceptive pills like Plan B to three per customer due to a surge in demand following the US Supreme Court decision overturning Roe v. Wade. Other chains, such as Walgreens, have not implemented purchase limits at this time, though some Walmart products have online purchase limits that may change with demand fluctuations. The increased demand for emergency contraception reflects preparations people are making in response to the ruling, which is expected to make abortions largely illegal in many states.

title: Federal Realty Pandemic Program Produced Permanent Deals for 50% of Tenants
summary: Don Wood, CEO of Federal Realty Investment Trust, discussed the company's temporary leasing program during the pandemic, which resulted in over half of the tenants transitioning to permanent deals. He also highlighted the acquisition of Kingstowne Towne Center in Virginia and the importance of ESG principles, noting the company's 13 megawatts of solar capacity.

title: Kroger's automated grocery delivery warehouse opens in Pleasant Prairie
summary: Kroger has opened a new automated grocery delivery warehouse in Pleasant Prairie, Wisconsin, in partnership with Ocado Group PLC. This facility is the fifth of its kind for Kroger and is expected to create approximately 250 jobs, serving customers in Wisconsin, northern Illinois, and northwest Indiana. The warehouse utilizes a robotic system called "The Hive" to efficiently sort and pack groceries for delivery.

title: Most Powerful Women 2022
summary: Cablefax celebrates its 2022 Most Powerful Women in Broadband in Media, recognizing top-performing female executives across various sectors. The magazine highlights "Glass Breakers" who have overcome barriers, along with Women’s Advancement Champions, a Mentor of the Year, and the "Rising Tide" Class, featuring up-and-coming women making significant contributions. The publication includes insights from honorees on their evolving definitions of success and experiences as the sole women in a room.

title: Unicard and Amdocs announce account-based ticketing platform
summary: Unicard and Amdocs have partnered to launch an account-based ticketing platform for multi-mode and multi-operator transportation services. The platform, introduced at the Transport Ticketing Global exhibition in London, integrates Unicard's ABT system with Amdocs' cloud-based payment platform to offer a seamless 'tap-in, tap-out' experience across various public transport options. Initially targeting city regions and local authorities in the UK, this collaboration aims to promote sustainable and flexible travel.

title: DISA looks to install 10GB ethernet line from Equinix data center to DHS facility
summary: The Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) is seeking bids to install and maintain a 10GB ethernet line connecting an Equinix data center in Dallas, Texas, to a Department of Homeland Security (DHS) facility in Pensacola, Florida. This initiative supports DHS's ongoing cloud migration efforts, which involve shifting workloads from their current data centers to cloud providers like AWS. The move comes amid continued spending on existing facilities and some controversy surrounding cloud contracts with human rights groups and Google employees protesting deals with ICE.

title: AWS: Amazon (AMZN) Cloud Unit on Course for $3 Trillion Value, Redburn Says
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) is projected by Redburn Ltd. to reach a $3 trillion valuation, a figure nearly triple Amazon.com Inc.'s current total market capitalization. Analyst Alex Haissl suggests AWS is so dominant that Amazon might eventually consider spinning it off from its slower-growing e-commerce business. The report initiates coverage on the cloud-computing industry but does not specify a timeline for AWS to achieve this valuation.

title: Self-driving truck firm Waymo to deliver goods for Wayfair on Interstate 45
summary: Waymo, Alphabet Inc.'s self-driving technology unit, is partnering with J.B. Hunt Transport Services to deliver Wayfair goods on Interstate 45 between Houston and Dallas. This six-week pilot program, starting in July, will involve autonomous Class 8 trucks with specialists monitoring operations in the cab. The partnership builds on previous successful tests and aims to integrate autonomous freight movement into supply chains to meet capacity needs.

title: BP, Shell to cover employee travel for treatment after Roe v. Wade
summary: BP PLC has joined Shell PLC in committing to cover employee travel expenses for healthcare treatment following the Supreme Court's overturning of Roe v. Wade. Both European oil producers updated their healthcare plans to extend benefits for women needing to travel for services, though neither explicitly named abortion. This move comes as other major companies like Amazon, JPMorgan Chase, Tesla, and Walt Disney also updated their policies to cover travel costs for out-of-state abortion services, while U.S. oil majors have largely remained silent.

title: The 13 Best Grill Brands
summary: This article identifies and reviews 13 top grill brands, highlighting what makes each manufacturer stand out in the market. It discusses various types of grills, including charcoal, gas, pellet, and griddles, outlining their price ranges, top products, and unique features. The selection criteria prioritize durability, performance, versatility, and availability across different retailers, catering to diverse user needs and budgets.

title: Corsair TC200 gaming chair review: "A great chair for both work and play"
summary: The Corsair TC200 gaming chair offers significant improvements over its predecessor, the T3 Rush, particularly for larger users with its wider seat and back, and internal lumbar support. Reviewer Frederick Hillinger praises its all-day comfort for both work and gaming, despite the lumbar support not being adjustable. The chair is highly recommended for its strong value, high-quality materials, and thoughtful design that incorporates user feedback.

title: Exploring Life & Business with Lily Sanchez of Lily Catherine
summary: Lily Sanchez, at just 13, launched her business, Lily Catherine, specializing in handmade jewelry before expanding into accessories, clothing, and decor. She discusses her journey from selling beaded bracelets to classmates to establishing an online presence, joining farmers' markets, and stocking products in local boutiques. Sanchez emphasizes overcoming challenges like balance and social media marketing while highlighting the crucial support from her community and family.

title: Frito-Lay CHRO: 'Everyone needs mental health support' | Human Resources Director
summary: Frito-Lay, a division of PepsiCo, Inc., is actively addressing the trucking industry's challenges, including high attrition and mental health concerns, by investing in its drivers' well-being. CHRO Patrick McLaughlin highlights the company's comprehensive approach, which includes competitive benefits, work-life balance initiatives, and robust mental health support programs like meQ and Spring Health. This strategy aims to improve retention and ensure Frito-Lay remains an employer of choice in a volatile labor market.

title: Is Augmented Reality the future of retail?
summary: Augmented Reality (AR) is poised to revolutionize the retail industry by improving customer experience and conversion rates. Using just a smartphone, AR allows customers to virtually try on products like jewelry, clothing, furniture, and even cars within their own physical environment. This technology helps consumers make more informed purchasing decisions and offers businesses a significant increase in sales conversion, even for physical showrooms utilizing "Magic Mirror" devices.

title: Cloudera embraces Apache Iceberg as cloud data lake evolves
summary: Cloudera has announced support for Apache Iceberg, an open-source cloud data lake table format, within its Cloudera Data Platform. This move signifies Cloudera's continued evolution from its Hadoop roots towards modern cloud data lake technology. The company believes Iceberg enhances its ability to work with various cloud providers and analytical engines, addressing the growing need for flexible and structured data lake solutions in enterprise environments.

title: How Nuuly is using technology to aid in sustainability tracking
summary: Nuuly, a clothing rental service by Urban Outfitters, is leveraging cloud-based technology, specifically Google Cloud, to track clothing items and enhance sustainability efforts. By understanding customer behavior and garment lifecycles through data analytics, Nuuly aims to reduce waste and improve efficiency. This initiative aligns with a broader retail trend where companies are prioritizing ESG efforts, though many struggle with implementation and measurement of sustainability.

title: Electronics companies dealing with a 'mountain of inventory'
summary: Samsung Electronics and LG Electronics are currently experiencing record-high inventory levels due to a significant decrease in demand for electronic devices globally. This oversupply, impacting everything from smartphones to home appliances, is leading companies to cut orders from suppliers, reduce working hours, and is expected to negatively affect earnings and balance sheets. The article highlights how factors like inflation, China's lockdown, and geopolitical tensions have weakened consumer sentiment, resulting in a "mountain of inventory" that needs to be consumed before market balance can be restored.

title: Amazon, Disney, AT&T Gave to Abortion Foes Like DeSantis While Vowing to Help Employees
summary: Amazon, Disney, and AT&T, despite pledging to cover travel costs for employees seeking reproductive medical care, have also contributed financially to anti-abortion governors and political figures like Ron DeSantis. State campaign-finance records show these corporate giants supported leaders actively working to reduce access to abortions, creating a contradiction between their public stances and political donations.
